biggest_catch: Unbabel publishes no per-task pay rate on its official pages — and access to paid work is rating-gated and workload-dependent, so even qualified editors can sit idle.
catches: No official published pay figure: the official help center describes how payments work but states no rate per task, per word, or per hour.

Zero guaranteed tasks — official help: 'if you are concerned that having a lower rating has lessened your access to paid tasks, this is possible - however it is much more likely that your evaluation has coincided with a fluctuation in workload for the whole community.'
Qualification gauntlet: application → language test (one attempt only; fail and the language pair is locked) → interface tour → skill test of five tasks, with no second try.
Your rating determines task access; editors with the highest ratings see tasks first.
Work is post-editing machine translation, not translation from scratch — effective hourly pay depends on editing speed.
Could not confirm the catalog's '$15' claim anywhere on official pages; third-party sources cite $8–$18/hr ranges but are not official.

c1.evidence: Unbabel is a real operating company (YC-backed, unbabel.com); official editor help center at help.unbabel.com loaded and indexed.

c2.evidence: Official help articles ('Getting started at Unbabel: a definitive guide', 'How does my rating affect my access to paid tasks?') describe the editor program and payment philosophy ('paid quickly, frequently and the full amount that they have earned'), but state no rate.

c3.evidence: Application and tests are free per the official guide; no signup fee mentioned.

c4.evidence: No official published pay figure found — the catalog's $15 claim could not be confirmed on unbabel.com or help.unbabel.com.

eligibility: Proficiency in 2+ languages; pass the application, a one-attempt language test, and a five-task skill test; only for languages Unbabel is actively recruiting.
notes: Read official help.unbabel.com articles via search index (2026-09-22): the definitive getting-started guide walks through application → language test (single attempt, pair locked on fail) → interface tour → skill test (5 tasks) → paid jobs; a separate article explains ratings gate task access and workloads fluctuate community-wide. The Editor's Hub page (unbabel.com/de/hub-for-editors) pitches joining the community with no pay figure. Searched for an official per-task/per-hour rate — none published. The '$15' catalog claim appears unsupported; only non-official sources (howtofindanonlinejob.com, copy.ai roundups) cite $8–$18/hr ranges.

s1.note: Single-attempt language test; locked language pair on failure; skill test has no retries; only actively-recruiting languages.

s2.note: Task access is rating-gated and fluctuates with community-wide workload; post-editing MT output, paid per task.

s3.note: Paid 'quickly, frequently and the full amount' per the official guide, but no schedule, method, or minimum published.

s4.note: No official earnings claim found — nothing to check for weasel words; the catalog's $15 is unverified.

s6.note: No concrete steps to a guaranteed payout exist — rejected per verdict rules, so steps omitted.
